rows.claim: If you count a subscription as still active on its last day, the count goes up by 2 and MRR rises by those two plans' prices
rows.evidence: The tool output shows "end on oct1: 2", so two subscriptions end on 2026-10-01. The code excludes them because their end_date is not after the day. Counting them as active on their last day would add 2 to the count, and MRR would rise by their plan prices. The first part of the claim is directly supported, and the second follows from it.

rows.claim: The data has no discounts or quantities to adjust for
rows.evidence: The CSV header, shown in the first tool call, has only sub_id, customer, plan, start_date and end_date. There are no discount or quantity columns. plans.json holds only plan prices.
